output.Title: Routing Information Protocol (RIP) - RFC 1058
output.Abstract: This document describes the Routing Information Protocol (RIP), version 1, which is a distance-vector protocol used for exchange of routing information among IP networks. RIP uses hop count as its metric.

Sections.Title: Introduction
Sections.Content: RIP is a distance-vector interior gateway protocol. This RFC defines version 1 of the protocol.

Sections.Title: Specifications for RIP Version 1
Sections.Content: This section provides technical details about RIP version 1, including message formats, timers, routing updates, triggered updates, and control functions.

Sections.Title: Message Format
Sections.Content: Details the format of RIP request and response messages, including fields such as command, version, update interval, check sum, and routing data.

Sections.Title: Timers
Sections.Content: Discusses RIP timers, including Update Timer and Invalid Timer.

Sections.Title: Routing Updates
Sections.Content: Explains how routers send routing updates to other directly connected routers. Includes discussion on split horizon reporting, poison reverse, and triggered updates.

Sections.Title: Control Functions
Sections.Content: Details optional administrative controls for managing the flow of RIP information, such as neighbor lists and destination address allow/disallow lists.
